summary: Adaptive window slippage causes batcher saturation and intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Acme Analytics began seeing sudden p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent request timeouts (504) for their dedicated cluster (acme-1) starting 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC. The pattern looks like repeated short bursts of elevated tail latency with periods of normal behavior between bursts.

Impact:
- User-facing API requests experiencing p99 up to ~3.4s (baseline ~120–200ms).
- Intermittent 504s observed at ~0.6-1.2% of requests during bursts.
- Affects endpoints: text-generation streaming and non-streaming.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: acme-1 (prod, us-east)
- Model variants: llama-2-13b-instruct (primary), fallback to redwood-v1-medium observed during some bursts
- Batcher: continuous adaptive batcher with linger/autotune enabled (customer-default tuning)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Steady low-per-connection QPS (~0.5–1 req/s) from many connections (hundreds).
2) Varying sequence lengths (short prompts and occasional long prompts) submitted.
3) After ~5–20 minutes of steady traffic, the batcher exhibits short-lived saturation events where queue length grows and flush latency spikes.
4) During those windows, p95/p99 climb and a subset of requests time out at the API gateway.

Observed behavior:
- Correlated metric: continuous_batcher.occupancy spikes to >0.9 for short intervals while batch flush latency metric increases dramatically.
- KV cache miss rate increases slightly during spikes; however, primary correlation is with batcher occupancy and linger time drift (batcher.linger_ms rising above configured limits for a subset of active queues).
- Logs show repeated micro-queue handoffs and an accumulation of pending requests on specific batcher shards.

Expected behavior:
- Adaptive batcher should maintain low linger for low-QPS flows and not produce sustained queue backlogs.

Logs & dashboards referenced:
- Grafana panel: /d/serve/latency-by-cluster?cluster=acme-1
- SLO dashboard: p95/p99 per-route (timestamps 2026-03-09 22:05–22:45 UTC)
- API gateway logs: /logs/customer/acme-1/2026-03-09

Additional notes:
- Customer reported temporary impact to product demos and asked for fast mitigation and timeline for permanent fix.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 - Support (Marcus Chen): Opened ticket after customer provided initial logs and Grafana links. Requested SRE triage and sample traces.

2026-03-10 12:22 - SRE (Elena Garcia): Correlated p99 spikes to continuous_batcher.occupancy and batcher.flush_latency. Spikes appear in specific batcher shards (shard-7, shard-11). No obvious hardware OOM or GPU errors. Requesting heap and queue metrics for affected workers.
2026-03-10 13:10 - Customer (Acme Analytics, Priya Rao): We can reproduce by running our staging load generator; attaching traffic patterns and sample payloads. Can you try a config change?

2026-03-10 13:45 - Support (Marcus Chen): Applied temporary mitigation (reduced batcher.max_batch_size, forced lower linger cap) in a single shard as a canary. Observed reduction in p99 for that shard within 3 minutes.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Engineer (Diego Morales): Preliminary hypothesis: adaptive window estimator drifts upward for low-QPS flows due to periodic long sequences, causing occupancy oscillator and transient shard-level saturation. Creating engineering ticket INT-4239 for long-term fix.

2026-03-12 15:05 - SRE (Elena Garcia): Rolled back adaptive linger thresholds to previous stable values across acme-1 and enabled temporary autoscale burst capacity. Customer confirmed latency returned to baseline in monitored window.
2026-03-12 16:25 - Customer (Acme Analytics, Priya Rao): Confirmed service stabilization; asked for root-cause write-up and permanent remediation ETA.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 12:30 - Pulled batcher shard metrics (/internal/metrics/batcher/shard/*). Observed intermittent linger_ms spikes on shards serving many small-connection flows.
2026-03-10 12:50 - Captured flamegraphs from serving runtime during a spike. CPU not saturated; latency concentrated in scheduling/wake-up paths inside the batch coalescer.
2026-03-10 13:00 - KV cache miss rate rose by ~8% during bursts but did not explain full tail; primary signal remains batcher occupancy and linger drift.
2026-03-10 13:30 - Canary change: set batcher.max_batch_size=32 -> p99 for canary shard down from ~3.2s to ~240ms; suggests oversized batches and delayed flushes amplified tail.

2026-03-11 08:00 - Reviewed recent infra rollout (infra PR #1189) that adjusted adaptive estimator damping parameters; temporal correlation exists between rollout and first customer reports (2026-03-09). Reverted damping in canary cluster for comparison.

2026-03-11 11:15 - Added extra telemetry: track per-connection linger and per-shard flush count. Early data shows a small subset of long sequences cause linger estimator to bias upward for many subsequent short requests.
2026-03-12 14:50 - Implemented cluster-wide temporary mitigations (lower linger cap, lower max_batch_size, enabled burst autoscale). Observed stabilization across all shards for acme-1.
2026-03-12 15:40 - Engineering triage: two follow-ups — fix estimator algorithm to be robust to infrequent long sequences (INT-4239), and add a canary detection alert for linger drift (INT-4240).
resolution:
Mitigation applied: reverted adaptive estimator damping to previous stable parameters and applied conservative batcher caps (max_batch_size=32, max_linger_ms=15) across acme-1; enabled temporary autoscale burst. Result: p95/p99 returned to baseline within monitoring window and 504 rate dropped to <0.1%.

Permanent remediation plan: engineering to implement estimator fix and add canary/alerting (INT-4239 & INT-4240). Postmortem and write-up to be added to Confluence (linked). Customer follow-up: scheduled technical review with Acme Analytics on 2026-03-17.
